name: Falfarren River
summary: The Falfarren River cuts through central Ashenvale, from Mount Hyjal toward the northern mountains of the Barrens. Its banks mark the divide between night elven lands and Horde outposts, where travelers face wild dangers and open conflict.

sections.title: A Contested Natural Boundary
sections.body: The Falfarren River descends from Mount Hyjal, spilling over waterfalls into Xavian before winding between Splintertree Post and Night Run. In ordinary weather, its waters are neither especially deep nor impassable. The river marks a rough boundary through central Ashenvale. Astranaar and the heart of the Kaldorei lands lie west; Horde camps and lumber operations lie east. The wooden bridges on the main road carry travelers into the contested forest, where patrols clash along the banks.

sections.title: Hazards in the Shallows
sections.body: The Falfarren River holds dangers beyond clashes between sentinels and grunts. Near Felfire Hill, corrupted bog beasts and aggressive water creatures prowl the muddy shallows. Rain can swell the currents. Dense canopies line both shores, where ambushes and skirmishes often spill into the stream.

faq.q: Where does the Falfarren River begin and end?
faq.answer: The Falfarren River begins in the heights of Mount Hyjal, then tumbles over waterfalls into the lake at Xavian. It winds southwest across Ashenvale before disappearing underground beneath the northern mountains of the Barrens.

faq.q: Why is the Falfarren River significant to the war in Ashenvale?
faq.answer: The Falfarren River marks a rough boundary between night elf and Horde control in central Ashenvale. Astranaar lies to the west, while the orc outpost of Splintertree Post and active Horde lumber operations lie to the east.

faq.q: What threats should travelers expect along the riverbanks?
faq.answer: Aggressive bog beasts prowl the shallows, especially near the corrupted lands around Felfire Hill. Patrols from both the Alliance and the Horde watch bridges and crossings, and skirmishes and ambushes can break out along the banks.

angles.text: For the Night Elves and their allies, crossing east over the Falfarren River brings you into the Horde's front lines near Splintertree Post.
For the Horde, the Falfarren River marks the western edge of your expansion from Splintertree Post. Fortified night elf territory lies beyond it.
